title: Letter 28 — On Consolation from God
attribution_note: Letter 28 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Who can comfort the sorrowful, save God alone? To draw sorrow out of the soul is not as to draw a splinter out of the body. This is God's work. From God must consolation be sought. And it is sought by earnest prayer. God grieves us, yet He is also merciful, according to the multitude of His mercy. *“Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and He shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the Lord.”* [Psalm 26:14] God does not leave those who endure without consolation, as a loving father does not leave his sons. He chastens them and has mercy; He smites and comforts. *“The expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever.”* [Psalm 9:19] When a mother or a father chastens thee — thou endurest, though it be painful: why then not endure, and the more so, when God, who is above our fathers and mothers, the Lord Himself, chastens us? Have ye forgotten the comforting apostolic word: *“For whom the Lord loveth He chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom He receiveth”*? [Hebrews 12:6]

sections.heading: My weakness, and counsel for you

pairs.en: I have written to you as much as I could, and thereby stirred both your soul and my own from despondency. Now I am already worn out in body. O that the soul were whole in a feeble body! You see that I write by another's hand, because I cannot write with my own.

You must strive to have useful books, and from them draw instruction and consolation; and pray to God as often as you can; but with guests associate rarely and with caution. For this is of little profit to him that would *“live godly”* [2 Timothy 3:12]: for what a man gathers in solitude, he loses among guests, and does like one who draws water with a sieve, or who draws with another vessel and spills it out again.

sections.heading: Remembrance of death and of eternity

pairs.en: You write: like dogs we shall turn *“to our own vomit”* [2 Peter 2:22]. But hear what the prophet cries to such: *“As for such as turn aside unto their crooked ways, the Lord shall lead them forth with the workers of iniquity.”* [Psalm 124:5] Remember often death, which comes unlooked-for and snatches a man in divers ways. Remember the judgment of Christ and the strict examination there. Remember eternal torment and the kingdom of heaven as often as you can. Not only every day, but every hour meditate upon these things. Such meditation will not suffer a man to turn aside from the good path. [see Sirach 7:29]

Temporal punishment touches a man and troubles him, and brings him into fear; and temporal blessedness cheers him. Shall eternal torment not touch, and terrify, and move our despondent heart? And shall not eternal blessedness kindle desire in our hearts? But this is the woe — that men forget these most needful things!...
